items.title: SPHMC D.7 proof edge: two Picard layers from a phase-state moment

source.anchor: Appendix D.2, Lemma D.4, equation D.7, layer argument on lines 2177–2181
source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang. Samplinglib expands one conditional two-layer moment edge; it is not the authors' original wording, the whole equation D.7, Lemma D.4, equation D.8 or an endorsement.

items.statement: Conditional on the separate run-wide phase-state second-moment estimate and the Chebyshev–Lobatto integrated-weight row bound, the actual stopped approximate-proximal computation used by the first Picard layer has integrable gradient queries, and those moments propagate through the finite weighted update to every second-layer center. All measurability and integrability obligations are explicit, and marginal Gaussian second moments suffice.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional Euclidean-compatible Borel space; C² normalized Hessian bounds kappa⁻¹I≼D²V≼I and a minimizer x* with ∇V(x*)=0.

A probability-space realization of one phase with E[‖X−x*‖²+‖P₀‖²]≤M for the post-refresh momentum P₀, including integrability; |t_i|≤1. The refresh adapter from the repeated-chain state remains separate.
Measurable innovations with integrable squared norm and E‖G_j‖²≤d; no independence premise is used in this conditional edge.
Absolute integrated-weight row sum at most S and parameters 0<eta≤c<1, eps>0.

formulae.label: Random first-layer query bound
formulae.tex: B=6M+3\varepsilon^2+3\eta d,\qquad \mathbb E\|\nabla V(q(Y_j^0)+\sqrt\eta G_j)\|^2\le B.

obligations.label: Actual measurable stopped proximal execution at every first-layer center
First-center and random proximal-gradient L2 estimates
Repeated Algorithm 3.1 law, run-wide state moment and post-refresh adapter (remaining)
Paper parameter substitution yielding the stated D.7 order (remaining)
Phase/call aggregation and D.8 total work (remaining)

bindings.boundary: Conditional two-layer L2 propagation for one realized phase. The repeated Algorithm 3.1 history law, the source's run-wide W2/state estimate, insertion of eta, eps, d, kappa and L_q, the final C*kappa*d*L_q^18 value, D.8, sampling accuracy and Theorem 5.1 remain unsupported red obligations.

assumption_deltas.source: The D.7 proof first invokes the run-wide state estimate from D.3 with q=2 and Lemma 4.16, then Algorithm 3.1 refreshes momentum before forming Y⁰.
assumption_deltas.lean: The realized X and post-refresh P₀ law and its integrable second-moment upper bound M are explicit premises.
assumption_deltas.reason: This freezes only the subsequent two-layer propagation. Construction of the repeated state law and the refresh-moment adapter remain separate visible obligations; the same constant is not silently reused.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper uses standard Gaussian innovations in R^d inside Algorithm 3.1.
assumption_deltas.lean: Each measurable innovation is required only to satisfy integrability and E‖G_j‖²≤finrank(E); no independence is assumed.
assumption_deltas.reason: The displayed moment calculation uses no independence. The future kernel/history theorem must separately construct the correct joint Gaussian law.

assumption_deltas.source: The paper states a universal C and suppresses the elementary two-layer constants.
assumption_deltas.lean: The conditional theorem records B=6M+3eps²+3eta*d and 4M+2S²B.
assumption_deltas.reason: These explicit sufficient constants follow from the same triangle/Cauchy–Schwarz route and are intended to be absorbed by the source's universal C after parameter insertion.

assumption_deltas.source: Algorithm 3.1 calls an approximate proximal routine and then forms its Picard interpolation layers.
assumption_deltas.lean: The theorem retains the exact finite-fuel interpreter equation and its measurable p,N,q witnesses, while abstracting only the current phase-state variables and finite node/weight data.
assumption_deltas.reason: The local execution semantics are real; only the repeated kernel/history law and source-specific node construction remain separate.

assumption_deltas.source: The source works in R^d under normalized strong-convexity and smoothness assumptions.
assumption_deltas.lean: A finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space and genuine C² Hessian inequalities are used.
assumption_deltas.reason: This includes the Euclidean source setting and makes genuine differentiability explicit instead of relying on totalized fderiv.
